units.source_text: [\[17\]](#part1336.html#w17) 白居易诗《夜闻歌者宿鄂州》：“

en.t: Bai Juyi's poem "Hearing a Singer at Night While Staying in Ezhou" says:

units.source_text: 夜泊鹦鹉洲，秋江月澄澈。

en.t: At night I moored by Parrot Islet; the autumn river and moon were clear and bright.

units.source_text: 邻船有歌者，发调堪愁绝。

en.t: On a neighboring boat there was someone singing; when she began her tune, the sorrow was almost unbearable.

units.source_text: 歌罢继以泣，泣声通复咽。

en.t: When the song ended, she went on weeping; her sobs carried through the night and broke again in choking sounds.

units.source_text: 寻声见其人，有妇颜如雪。

en.t: Following the sound, I saw the singer: a woman whose face was as white as snow.

units.source_text: 独倚帆樯立，娉婷十七八。

en.t: She stood alone leaning against the mast, graceful and slender, about seventeen or eighteen.

units.source_text: 夜泪似珍珠，双双堕明月。

en.t: Her tears in the night were like pearls, falling two by two in the bright moonlight.

units.source_text: 借问谁家妇，歌泣何凄切？

en.t: I ventured to ask whose wife she was, and why her singing and weeping were so heartbroken.

units.source_text: 一问一沾襟，低眉终不说。”

en.t: At each question she only wet her robe with tears, lowered her brows, and in the end said nothing."
